papers.title: Best1 shapes the depth and stability of NREM sleep.
papers.summary: Using Best1 knockout mice and EEG/EMG polysomnography, the study found that the astrocytic calcium-activated anion channel Best1 is required for deep NREM sleep, as knockouts showed shorter deep NREM bouts, reduced delta power, and altered vigilance-state transitions despite preserved total sleep time.

papers.title: Slow-Wave Enhancement Reduces Axonal Injury in Murine Traumatic Brain Injury.
papers.summary: Developed an adapted weight-drop mouse traumatic brain injury model compatible with EEG/EMG recording that shows cognitive impairment, EEG abnormalities, and diffuse axonal injury, and found that sodium oxybate treatment over the first 3 days after trauma increased slow-wave activity and reduced axonal injury, whereas chemogenetic modulation of basal forebrain cholinergic neurons did not reduce slow-wave activity.

papers.title: Neural mitochondria size is negatively correlated with sleep duration.
papers.summary: By measuring neural mitochondrial cross-sections from electron micrographs across 51 mammalian species, the study found that average neural mitochondrial area decreases roughly exponentially with sleep duration (r = -0.76), suggesting mitochondrial size as a cellular determinant of sleep duration.

papers.title: Short sleep for whom? Toward a personalized definition of sleep duration adequacy.
papers.summary: This editorial argues for a personalized definition of sleep duration adequacy, moving beyond universal recommendations to consider individual sleep needs and characteristics.

papers.title: State-dependent gating of sensory and cortical inputs by median raphe neurons
papers.summary: Characterized state-dependent responses of serotonergic, Vglut3 glutamatergic, and GABAergic median raphe neurons to sensory and cortical stimulation in vivo, showing larger responses during slow-wave sleep than wakefulness, with 5-HT neurons suppressed and Vglut3/GABAergic neurons activated by sensory stimuli, and optogenetic prefrontal input inhibiting 5-HT while exciting Vglut3 neurons during slow-wave sleep.

papers.title: Multiple platform-induced sleep restriction disrupts time-of-day-dependent corticosterone and leukocyte profiles in C57BL/6 mice.
papers.journal: Neurobiology of sleep and circadian rhythms
papers.summary: In male C57BL/6 mice subjected to subchronic sleep restriction via the multiple-platform procedure, 24-hour diurnal profiles revealed significant time-of-day-dependent differences in serum corticosterone and granulocyte-enriched percentages at specific Zeitgeber times, without altering daily mean corticosterone or total white blood cell counts.

papers.title: Comparison of Infradian and Circadian Rhythms in Laboratory Rodents.
papers.journal: Journal of experimental zoology. Part A, Ecological and integrative physiology
papers.summary: Monitoring locomotor activity in three rodent species and using Lomb-Scargle spectral analysis, the study found robust circadian rhythms in all animals, while infradian rhythms (5- and 10-day ranges) were extremely low in mice and moderate in gerbils and squirrels, with infradian strength less than 10% of circadian strength.

papers.title: iEEG Can Help EEG: Improving Clinical Scalp EEG Analysis through Intracranial Priors
papers.summary: Proposes ReBrain, a reprogramming framework that fits a signal-to-signal model on intracranial EEG alone, freezes it as a cross-modal prior, and transfers it upstream of scalp EEG models without pairing or fine-tuning. ReBrain consistently improved host models across recordings from multiple hospitals and architecture families, with analysis attributing gains to neural structure carried by iEEG rather than architecture.

papers.title: Deciphering the impact of chronological age on sleep stage transition dynamics for disorder classification.
papers.summary: Investigates how chronological age affects sleep stage transition probability (STP) features for sleep disorder classification, comparing age-agnostic, age-involved, and age-specific machine learning models across single-night hypnograms. Age-involved models improved accuracy and F1-score by about 2-4% over age-agnostic models (which reached roughly 85%), while age-specific models improved by about 8-12%, especially in subjects aged 60 and older.

papers.title: Toward Closed-Loop Cognitive Modulation in Alzheimer's Disease: BCI-Relevant Evidence and a Translational Roadmap.
papers.summary: Presents a targeted narrative review mapping brain-computer interface and closed-loop-relevant evidence in Alzheimer's disease and mild cognitive impairment, organizing sensing, control, and intervention modules into a translational roadmap. The authors conclude that reliable decoding of waking cognitive states, broader controller utility, and durable clinical benefit remain unvalidated, and propose early trial designs comparing adaptive policies to matched fixed delivery.

papers.title: Associations of sleep architecture, sleep fragmentation, and hypoxia-related parameters with cognitive frailty in older patients with hypertension and obstructive sleep apnea: a cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional study of 240 hospitalized older patients with hypertension and obstructive sleep apnea examining associations of polysomnography-derived sleep architecture, fragmentation, and hypoxia parameters with cognitive frailty. After adjustment, shorter N3 sleep duration and lower minimum oxygen saturation were independently negatively associated with cognitive frailty, while higher arousal index was independently positively associated.

papers.title: When impulsivity goes wrong: Circadian timing distinguishes which night shift workers succeed and fail.
papers.summary: Assessed whether phase angle between circadian timing (dim-light melatonin onset, DLMO) and task time predicts impulsivity on the Stop Light Task in 30 night-shift workers. Greater phase angle was associated with worse performance (more crashes) and worse risk strategy, while phase angle did not predict action bias, and post-hoc analysis showed greater sleepiness predicted reduced action bias.

papers.title: Effects of housing system on locomotor activity and circadian rhythmicity in llamas (Lama glama).
papers.summary: Using neck-mounted triaxial accelerometers and 24-h cosinor analysis in ten adult llamas, the study found that continuous housing without pasture access reduced mean locomotor activity by ~33% in males and ~47% in females versus grazing-confinement, and significantly lowered MESOR, amplitude, rhythm robustness, and circadianity indices while preserving a stable 24-h period with early-afternoon acrophases.

papers.title: Knockdown of KCNQ2 in CA1 reshapes epilepsy-related limbic network rhythms and reduces spontaneous exploratory behavior in mice.
papers.summary: AAV-shRNA knockdown of KCNQ2 in mouse hippocampal CA1 increased calcium activity across glutamatergic, GABAergic, SST+, and PV+ neurons, produced a biphasic EEG pattern (reduced low-frequency power and connectivity during latency, then hypersynchronization during severe seizures), and biased phase-amplitude coupling toward the basolateral amygdala, accompanied by reduced exploratory, open-arm, novel-object, and social behaviors that retigabine partially alleviated.

papers.title: Ideal sleep duration as a potential explanation of the bimodal chronotype: An exploratory study.
papers.summary: Reanalyzed questionnaire data from 1583 children/adolescents and 2115 adults to test whether bimodal chronotypes represent a distinct circadian typology category or a byproduct of ideal sleep duration, finding bimodal types overrepresented among short and long sleepers and underrepresented among medium sleepers, suggesting bimodality may reflect individual differences in ideal sleep duration.

papers.title: In vivo probabilistic atlas mapping reveals brainstem nuclei volume increases in idiopathic REM sleep behavior disorder.
papers.summary: Segmenting 54 brainstem nuclei with the Brainstem Navigator atlas in 3D T1-weighted MRI from 178 iRBD patients and 111 controls (PPMI), the study found enlarged relative volumes of the left cuneiform nucleus, left lateral parabrachial nucleus, and left superior medullary reticular formation; the latter two correlated with RBDSQ and autonomic/affective/cognitive indicators, and a combined diagnostic model reached AUC 0.674.

papers.title: Distinct trajectories of 24-hour sleep duration and subsequent functional limitations in older adults: a national longitudinal cohort study.
papers.summary: In 4,999 CHARLS adults aged ≥50 without baseline functional limitations, latent class mixed models identified Stable Moderate (56.5%), Progressively Short (13.5%), and Progressively Long (30.0%) 24-hour sleep trajectories; the Progressively Short trajectory predicted higher risks of ADL (RR 1.34) and IADL (RR 1.22) limitations at Wave 5, while the Progressively Long trajectory was associated with severe ADL and IADL limitations.

papers.title: Signatures of Performance Monitoring in Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder and At-risk Groups: Midfrontal Theta Predicts Divergent Behavioral Adaptation.
papers.journal: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging
papers.summary: In 180 adults (46 OCD, 39 first-degree relatives, 39 with adverse childhood experiences, 56 controls) performing an arrowhead flanker task with EEG, OCD showed enhanced error-related midfrontal theta and prolonged post-error slowing, with single-trial theta predicting slower, less accurate subsequent performance in OCD but improved performance in controls; at-risk groups did not differ from controls.

papers.title: Exploratory Pilot Randomized Crossover Study of Transcutaneous Vagus Nerve Stimulation on Sleep Quality and Mood in Healthy Adults.
papers.summary: In a randomized, double-blind, crossover pilot trial of 29 healthy adults, active transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation (vs sham) produced a statistically significant but modest reduction in PSQI-K subjective sleep quality scores without exceeding the minimal clinically important difference; no significant effects emerged for BDI-II, HAM-D, or group-level HRV indices, and the intervention was safe and well tolerated.

papers.title: Diurnal cortisol, perceived sleep quality, actigraphic sleep and depression: an exploratory pilot in patients with head and neck cancer.
papers.summary: In an exploratory pilot of 40 head and neck cancer patients, poorer perceived sleep quality (PSQI) correlated with greater depressive symptoms (r=0.64), flatter diurnal cortisol slopes (r=0.48), and higher evening cortisol (r=0.40), whereas actigraphy-derived sleep parameters showed no significant associations with depression or cortisol indices.

papers.title: Circadian rhythm in the atrioventricular node - in electrophysiology, contractility, metabolism, intracellular signalling and extracellular matrix
papers.summary: In mouse and human atrioventricular nodes, the authors showed a day-night rhythm in PR interval and identified a local circadian clock, with Bmal1 knockout reducing the PR-interval rhythm by ~43-52% and Kcnj5 knockout ruling out a major vagal role. Rhythmic transcripts, proteins (~15% of 4,186), ion channels, and reduced L-type Ca2+ current during sleep, supported by computer modeling, were found to underlie slowed nodal conduction at night.

papers.title: Immediate Return or Overnight Stay? Sleep Responses by Postmatch Travel Strategy and Match Participation in Professional Football.
papers.summary: In an observational repeated-measures field study of 19 English Premier League players across 10 European away fixtures, sleep quality dropped on match and subsequent nights versus prematch; overnight stay yielded shorter absolute sleep but a clearer next-night rebound in quality and duration, while immediate return showed no rebound, and match participation moderated sleep duration.

papers.title: Flavonoids quercetin and fisetin activate circadian clock and inhibit adipocyte development and hypertrophy.
papers.journal: American journal of physiology. Cell physiology
papers.summary: This study shows that RORα activation (synthetic agonist or ectopic expression) inhibits adipogenesis, and that flavonoids quercetin and fisetin stimulate RORα transcriptional activity and clock oscillation, suppressing preadipocyte differentiation and lipid storage; in vivo, quercetin attenuated adipocyte hypertrophy and improved insulin sensitivity while fisetin showed less pronounced effects.

papers.title: Adoption of Routine Intraoperative Raw EEG at a Quaternary Pediatric Centre.
papers.summary: A retrospective single-center study of 26,168 pediatric anesthetic records found intraoperative raw EEG use rose from 17.8% to 28.4% over the study period, with wide provider variation (median 18.1%, range 0.9%-79.5%) that case mix explained only weakly (pseudo R2=0.064), indicating individual practice patterns drove uptake.

papers.title: Development and EEG Assessment of a Virtual Reality Replica of a Prior Real Multisensory Environment Intervention.
papers.summary: Developed a virtual reality replica (V-MSE) of a prior real multisensory environment intervention and characterized EEG spectral and nonlinear responses in 31 healthy participants pre- and post-exposure. The alpha/beta ratio increased significantly in both settings; in the V-MSE, frontal theta and theta/beta ratio also rose while relative gamma power and Lempel-Ziv complexity fell, supporting feasibility but not yet equivalence of V-MSEs.

papers.title: Component specific sleep-cognition associations in ICU professionals in India.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 45 rotating-shift ICU professionals, testing 63 PSQI-component × MoCA-item correlations with Benjamini-Hochberg correction and confounder adjustment, only daytime dysfunction remained associated with the attention-executive composite (rho = -0.43, corrected P = 0.026; adjusted beta = -0.94). The authors argue for a component-specific rather than global approach to sleep-related cognitive risk in critical care staff.

papers.title: SIRT7 Aggravates Chronic Sleep Deprivation-Induced Cognitive Impairment and Neuronal Apoptosis via Decreasing Succinylation and Cascaded Ubiquitylation of NFL.
papers.summary: Using a rat chronic sleep deprivation model with hippocampal ubiquitinomics and succinylomics, the study shows SIRT7 desuccinylates neurofilament light (NFL) at K370, suppressing cascaded ubiquitylation and enabling NFL accumulation, which drives cognitive impairment and neuronal apoptosis. SIRT7 inhibition or NFL knockdown attenuated these deficits, implicating SIRT7-NFL succinylation/ubiquitylation in insomnia-related cognitive decline.

papers.title: Sleep Deprivation Exacerbates Pulpal Inflammation and Impairs Repair Through Dysregulated Neutrophil Activity in Rats.
papers.summary: In rat models of sleep deprivation, pulpal inflammation and repair were assessed across baseline, LPS-induced pulpitis, and direct pulp capping settings, showing disrupted pulpal homeostasis, impaired hard tissue bridge formation, and later necrosis with apical periodontitis. Transcriptomics and neutrophil analyses implicated enhanced neutrophil accumulation/activation and neutrophil elastase, since neutrophil depletion or NE inhibition (Sivelestat) reduced inflammation and tissue damage.

papers.title: A novel theta-frequency tACS approach for major depressive disorder: Initial findings from an open-label pilot study.
papers.summary: This open-label pilot study delivered 20 sessions of individualized theta-frequency tACS (1.5 mA, 20 min) to prefrontal cortex during working memory tasks in 11 adults with moderate-to-severe MDD, with 10 completers. MADRS scores fell significantly from baseline through follow-up, with endpoint response/remission rates of 80%/60% and follow-up rates of 80%/70%, and greater increases in individualized theta power associated with greater symptom reduction.

papers.title: Report-derived interictal epileptiform discharge burden is associated with 7-day antiseizure medication decisions after pediatric video electroencephalography.
papers.summary: In a single-center retrospective cohort of 216 pediatric video-EEG report episodes, a three-level interictal epileptiform discharge burden abstracted from report wording showed strong inter-rater agreement (κ=0.975) and a graded association with new antiseizure medication initiation within 7 days (13.0%, 42.9%, 70.0% across none, low, and moderate-to-high burden; adjusted OR 2.89 per grade). Exploratory treatment intensification in established epilepsy also showed an association (OR 4.73) but with inconsistent complementary analyses, and causality was not established.

papers.title: Evidence for decoder-label-regime-dependent effects of complementary leaky integrate-and-fire temporal-state decoding in motor-imagery EEG.
papers.summary: Holding ATCNet and FBCNet EEG representations fixed, the study tested complementary leaky integrate-and-fire (CLIF)-family temporal-state decoders across BCI2a, OpenBMI, BCI2b, and BNCI2015-001. SEW-CLIF exceeded ANN-SEW by 10.082 pp on BCI2a and 5.470 pp on OpenBMI under cross-entropy-only training, but the advantage attenuated as decoder labels increased; exact-gradient Soft-CLIF also outperformed ANN-SEW, and matched temporal readout largely reduced the differences.

papers.title: Neurophysiological and Sleep-Related Effects of a Cosmetic Shampoo and Conditioner Regimen in Adults with Scalp Discomfort: A Pilot Study.
papers.summary: In a single-arm observational pilot of 20 adults with scalp discomfort and mild sleep disturbance using a cosmetic shampoo/conditioner regimen, EEG showed improved mood valence and sleepiness and all four sleep questionnaires improved, with scalp itch intensity down 49.1% and discomfort days down 40.6%. An exploratory post hoc subgroup with below-average baseline deep sleep showed a 20.6% increase in deep sleep duration, a hypothesis-generating finding.

papers.title: Joint associations of sleep duration and screen time with mental health symptoms among 10,620 Chinese university students: An exploratory cross-sectional dose-response analysis.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 10,620 Chinese university students, short sleep (<7 h/day) combined with high screen time (>8 h/day) was associated with higher odds of depression (OR 1.68), anxiety (OR 1.86), and stress (OR 2.31) versus a reference profile; exploratory physical activity dose-response patterns varied across sleep-screen profiles.

papers.title: Distinct cortical functional network alterations in internet gaming disorder and alcohol use disorder: A resting-state EEG graph theory analysis.
papers.summary: Resting-state EEG with source reconstruction and graph theory in 49 patients with internet gaming disorder, 48 with alcohol use disorder, and 54 controls showed IGD had higher beta-band global clustering coefficient and strength than AUD and controls, with increased beta-band nodal measures in parietal and limbic regions and lower bilateral superior frontal gyrus measures in AUD than IGD.

papers.title: The endothelial PECAM1-CXCR4 axis amplifies neutrophil degranulation to exacerbate sleep-deprived periodontitis: a systems-level framework for comorbidity therapy.
papers.summary: Integrating NHANES/KNHANES epidemiology, clinical samples, multi-omics, and mouse/cell models, this study identified an endothelial PECAM1–neutrophil CXCR4 axis in which PECAM1–CXCL12 interaction limits ligand availability, driving compensatory CXCR4 upregulation and excessive neutrophil degranulation that exacerbates sleep-deprivation-associated periodontitis. Curcumin was computationally and experimentally validated as a dual PECAM1/CXCR4 modulator that reduced periodontal destruction and was associated with partial NREM sleep recovery in comorbid mice.

papers.title: [Weight Management Strategies for Children and Adolescents: From Behavioral Correction to Systematic Prevention and Control].
papers.journal: Sichuan da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Sichuan University. Medical science edition
keywords: Intensive Health Behavior and Lifestyle Treatment
papers.summary: This review applies a three-level nested framework of individuals, environment, and policy to summarize evidence on Intensive Health Behavior and Lifestyle Treatment (IHBLT) for pediatric overweight/obesity and to identify core challenges such as balancing weight reduction with growth, sarcopenic obesity, and sleep health. It proposes three priority research directions for China: a localized IHBLT dose-response model, metabolically healthy versus unhealthy obesity phenotyping for stratified assessment, and dynamic growth-trajectory early-warning algorithms from school physical examination data.

papers.title: Mediators of the association between physical activity and depressive symptoms in youth: a systematic review and meta-analytic structural equation modelling.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analytic structural equation modelling study synthesized 87 observational studies (39 in the quantitative mediation subset) to identify mediators linking physical activity to depressive symptoms in youth aged 6-27 years. Physical activity was inversely associated with depressive symptoms (r = -0.234, 95% CI -0.281 to -0.187) with substantial heterogeneity, and MASEM supported indirect associations through psychological resilience (ab = -0.108), self-esteem (ab = -0.134), and social support (ab = -0.127), interpreted as statistical rather than causal pathways.

papers.title: Harnessing Circadian Resilience for Demand-Flexible Controlled Environment Agriculture
papers.summary: Using historical electricity market and wind-generation data, the authors tested demand-flexible photoperiod strategies (demand-side response events, cost-optimised and wind-optimised lighting) in controlled environment agriculture, finding preserved circadian rhythms and minimal effects on fresh or dry weight in basil, lettuce, mustard greens, and rocket. The results support demand-side energy flexibility in total controlled environment agriculture without substantial crop productivity losses.

papers.title: Correction: Circadian rhythms and sleep disturbances: a conceptual perspective with implications for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.
papers.summary: This is a published erratum correcting a conceptual perspective article on circadian rhythms and sleep disturbances in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease; no abstract or substantive findings are supplied.

papers.title: Comparing Fatigue Assessment Tools in Hemodialysis: Implications for Nephrology Practice From the Technology Assisted Stepped-Collaborative-Care Trial.
papers.summary: In 160 hemodialysis patients from a randomized controlled trial, SONG-HD-fatigue and PROMIS-fatigue showed psychometric properties comparable to FACIT-F, with strong correlations to related outcomes. However, only PROMIS-fatigue and FACIT-F detected significant treatment differences at 3 months, while SONG-HD-fatigue did not capture treatment response.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
